::: {.hero}
# Glossaries for Quarto, the way LaTeX does them {.hero-title}

Write a key in double square brackets, a [[wiki-link]] borrowed from Obsidian.
Students and other web readers hover over the term, or tap it on a phone, and
see its definition. The PDF uses LaTeX's `glossaries` package. Both come from
one vocabulary that you write in YAML.

```bash
quarto add brenobeirigo/quarto-glossary
```

[Get started](getting-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Ways to define terms](define-terms.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/brenobeirigo/quarto-glossary){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
:::

## Try it

Hover over the dotted words, or press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to reach them with the
keyboard.

::: {.demo-grid}
::: {.demo-pane}
[You write]{.demo-label}

```markdown
A [[doi]] identifies the dataset. Its
[[metadata]] record the [[sample-size]].
Cite the [[doi]] in the paper.
```
:::

::: {.demo-pane .demo-output}
[Readers see]{.demo-label}

A [[doi]] identifies the dataset. Its [[metadata]] record the [[sample-size]].
Cite the [[doi]] in the paper.
:::
:::

The first reference to the acronym printed the long form and the
abbreviation. The second printed the abbreviation alone. LaTeX calls this the
[[first-use]] rule, and the extension applies it on the web too.

## Why I built it

I write course notes and research papers in Quarto. [[latex]] has had the
`glossaries` package for years. You define a term or an acronym once. The first use of an acronym expands it, later uses
abbreviate it, and the list at the end of the document contains exactly the
entries you cited. I wanted the same thing in Quarto. The Quarto extensions I
found each covered part of it, so I wrote this one.

In teaching, a student meets a term and gets its definition at that word,
without leaving the page. A course can share one vocabulary, and an exercise
can carry its own terms into whichever chapter or exam includes it. In a
paper, acronyms and term lists work as they do in LaTeX.

I borrowed the brackets from Obsidian, where `[[Note name]]` links one note to
another. I use them for terms. `[[key]]` refers to an entry, and
`[[key|other text]]` changes the words on the page, as in an Obsidian link.

## Define terms where they fit

::: {.panel-tabset}

### In the document

Put the entries in the [[front-matter]]. The lesson is then one `.qmd` file
with nothing else to ship.

```yaml
---
title: Reading a confidence interval
filters: [glossary]
glossary:
  entries:
    - id: ci
      kind: acronym
      short: CI
      long: confidence interval
      definition: A range computed from a sample. Over repeated samples, a
        stated share of such ranges contains the true value.
---

A 95% [[ci]] for the mean heart rate is 65.2 to 70.8 bpm.
```

[See a lesson built this way, in HTML and PDF](demos/front-matter.qmd).

### In one file

Keep every term in one [[yaml|short]] file and point each document or the
whole project at it.

```yaml
# _quarto.yml or the document's front matter
filters: [glossary]
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
```

```yaml
# glossary.yml
entries:
  - id: sample-size
    term: sample size
    symbol: $n$
    definition: The number of units included in an analysis.
```

This manual keeps its vocabulary in
[`docs/glossary.yml`](https://github.com/brenobeirigo/quarto-glossary/blob/main/docs/glossary.yml).

### In several files

Split the vocabulary by topic or by course. [[json|short]] works too.

```yaml
glossary:
  path: [statistics.yml, acronyms.yml, course-2026.json]
```

Identical copies of a key merge. Two different meanings stop the render and name both sources.

### File plus page terms

Share a course vocabulary and add terms that only one lecture needs.

```yaml
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
  entries:
    - id: bootstrap
      term: bootstrap
      definition: Resampling the data with replacement to estimate
        the variability of a statistic.
```

### Website or book

Set the options once in `_quarto.yml` and give the lists their own page.
References on every other page then link to that page.

```yaml
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
  html-glossary-page: glossary.qmd
```

```markdown
<!-- glossary.qmd -->
::: {.glossary include-unused="true"}
:::
```

See this manual's [Glossary](glossary.qmd) page.
:::

## HTML and PDF from one source

::: {.demo-grid}
::: {.demo-pane}
[HTML]{.demo-label}

::: {.callout-note title="Balloons escape callouts and tables"}
A [[doi]] identifies a dataset, an article, or a report. The balloon is
attached to the page body, so this callout cannot clip it.
:::

| Context | Reference |
|---|---|
| Table cell | [[sample-size]] |
| Another cell | [[metadata]] |
: A caption can define [[reproducible-research]] too.
:::

::: {.demo-pane}
[PDF]{.demo-label}

[![The demo lesson rendered to PDF. The acronym expands on first use and the lists come from glossaries-extra.](images/pdf-output.png){.pdf-shot fig-alt="Two PDF pages. The first holds a short statistics lesson where the standard error and the confidence interval expand on first use. The second holds an Acronyms list with CI and SE and a Glossary list with confidence level, population mean, and sample mean."}](demos/front-matter.pdf)
:::
:::

The PDF uses `glossaries-extra` with the `long-short-desc` acronym style by
default. `makeindex` and `bib2gls` are available for theses and books. Details
are in [LaTeX and PDF output](latex-output.qmd). Word and Typst output get plain
references and the generated lists, with no balloons or `glossaries` package.

## Catching mistakes

A mistyped key stops the render and gives the file, the line, and the nearest
defined key, the way an unresolved cross-reference would:

```console
glossary: unknown glossary key [[sample-sise]] in chapter-2.qmd:41; did you mean [[sample-size]]?
```

If you work with an AI agent, the vocabulary is a plain file it can read. The
check covers `[[key]]` references only, so it won't stop anyone from paraphrasing
a term in plain text. See [Writing with agents](agents.qmd).

## How it compares

::: {.table-scroll}
| | Quarto Glossary | LaTeX `glossaries-extra` | [quarto-glossary](https://github.com/debruine/quarto-glossary) | [acronyms](https://github.com/rchaput/acronyms) | [glossary (R)](https://github.com/debruine/glossary) |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Runs in Quarto | ✓ | PDF only, by hand | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ through R |
| Reference syntax | `[[key]]` | `\gls{key}` | `{{</* glossary key */>}}` | `\acr{key}` | `` `r glossary("key")` `` |
| Terms in a YAML or JSON file | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Terms in the front matter | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Hover definitions on the web | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Definition on keyboard focus | ✓ | n/a | not documented | n/a | not documented |
| Generated list | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Separate acronym and term lists | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | acronyms only | ✗ |
| Acronym expands on first use | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Plural and capitalized forms | ✓ | ✓ | custom text only | plurals | custom text only |
| Native `glossaries` package in PDF | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| `makeindex` and `bib2gls` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Unknown key | stops the render | stops the build | empty definition | warning, or error if set | warning |
| Markdown, math, and citations in definitions | ✓ | ✓ (as LaTeX) | plain text | preview branch only | plain text in popups |
| Extra runtime | none | TeX tools | none | none | R |
: Glossary and acronym tools for Quarto, checked against each project's documentation in October 2026. {.compare-table}
:::

[qmd-lab/glossary](https://github.com/qmd-lab/glossary) is left out because it
collects definition blocks into one section and has no in-text references. If
a cell is wrong, [open an issue](https://github.com/brenobeirigo/quarto-glossary/issues)
and I will fix it.
